_comment: ESP32-C5-WROOM-1-N8R8 -- 8 MB flash, 8 MB quad PSRAM.  Used by envs esp32-c5-wroom-1-n8r8-00 and -01 (two physical units).  EXISTS BECAUSE N8R4 AND N8R8 ARE DIFFERENT BOARD TYPES AND MUST NOT SHARE A DEFINITION.  The pinned pioarduino platform (55.03.311) ships esp32-c5-devkitc-1, -n4, -n8r4 and -n16r4 -- no N8R8 -- so an N8R8 board has no stock definition to use and this file is it. || READ THIS BEFORE YOU DELETE IT AGAIN.  An earlier version of this comment justified the file with a MEASUREMENT THAT WAS FALSE: that building an N8R8 with the n8r4 definition 'silently gives the runtime half the PSRAM the board actually carries'.  It does not.  Verified on hardware 2026-09-11: an N8R8 board built against the stock n8r4 definition reports the full `PSRAM free: 7917236 / 8388608`.  NO BOARD JSON DECLARES A PSRAM SIZE -- there is no such field in this file or in any stock one -- because ESP-IDF sizes PSRAM by probing the chip at boot (B338). || SO WHY KEEP THE FILE?  Because a board definition NAMES A BOARD TYPE.  N8R4 and N8R8 are different hardware, and an N8R8 env declaring `board = esp32-c5-devkitc1-n8r4` is wrong in the record even when it is harmless in the bytes -- it misreports the part in build logs, in the `name` string, and to anything that reads `board` to infer memory.  The correct reason to keep a separate type is that it IS a separate type; the false reason was a mechanism that does not exist. Both can be true at once, and conflating them is how this file got marked obsolete on 2026-09-11 and then restored the same day. || WHAT IS ACTUALLY DIFFERENT HERE vs the stock n8r4 file: the `name` string, and `-DARDUINO_ESP32C5_DEV` in extra_flags.  Every other build-affecting field is identical, and that is EXPECTED, not a sign the file is redundant -- PSRAM size is simply not expressible here.
_psram_note: QUAD, not octal.  The C5 has no octal PSRAM part: memory_type is qio_qspi and psram_type is qio. Do not copy the S3-EYE's qio_opi here -- the S3 is the only chip in this tree with octal PSRAM, and an opi setting on a quad part fails at PSRAM INIT, which presents as a boot loop rather than as a configuration error.  SIZE IS NOT SET HERE AND CANNOT BE: the 8 MB in this file's `name` is documentation of the hardware, not configuration.  It was measured off both boards, not read off a part number.
name: Espressif ESP32-C5-WROOM-1-N8R8 (8 MB Flash Quad, 8 MB PSRAM Quad, RISC-V RV32)
